outlook.statement: The company has taken various steps to improve its strategies for higher market penetration and for increasing revenue realizations.

India's cement industry projected to grow at CAGR of 6.5% from 2026 to 2031 reaching 650 million metric tonnes per annum by 2031. Cement makers project 7-8% growth in FY27 driven by infra spending, housing demand, and urbanization despite West Asia headwinds.

Global economic growth for 2026 projected around 3.0% with inflation expected to fall but US inflation returning to target gradually. Growth resilient as technology and adaptability offset trade policy headwinds.
India GDP growth forecast at 6.5% in FY27, reflecting moderation from FY26 (7.6%). Strong economic fundamentals and reform initiatives helped limit impact of global disruptions.

Company initiated measures like selling certain cement products in Chettinad Brand to parent company, likely to result in gradual increase in capacity utilization and improve sales performance and profitability.
LCA will be planned and conducted in future.
Use of renewable energy is being explored. Process will be refined in coming years for value chain partner assessment. Scope 3 emissions monitoring and reporting will be initiated going forward.

competitive landscape in the cement industry
Raw material risk: Dependence on limestone and other raw materials; price uncertainty due to climatic conditions, commodity fluctuations, government policies, competition
Competition risk: Highly competitive industry dominated by large pan-India manufacturers; competition on price, quality, brand
Risk of change in Government policies: Reliance on infrastructure/housing demand; any pullback in government initiatives causes recession in cement industry
Power and fuel cost risk: Energy intensive industry; rise in international coal prices adversely impacts operating costs
Logistics Risk: Dependence on road transportation; rising diesel prices increase costs
Marketing Risk: Intense competition may adversely impact market share, sales volume, profitability
Information Technology Risk: Dependence on ERP and automated manufacturing; cyber security threats
Talent Management: Attrition and non-availability of required talent; challenges in recruiting, training, retaining talent
